newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom to cut planned capex by $500 mln.
newsitem.headline: Telecom to cut planned capex by $500 mln.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Tuesday it aimed to progressively remove NZ$500 million from its previously planned capital expenditure programme between now and the end of the 1999/2000 financial year.
The aim is part of a plan called "Performance 2000", which Telecom unveiled after reporting a first quarter profit result of $188 million, up from 177.1 million in the previous comparable period.

"Performance 2000 will improve Telecom's customer service because we will be working smarter. It will improve our performance as a business by reducing both ongoing overheads and capital expenditure," Telecom chief executive Roderick Deane said.
He said the benefits of the plan should start to be seen from the second half of this financial year but would be concentrated in the following two years.
Deane said Telecom planned to recognise future expenditure on implementing Performance 2000 as incurred.

"Performance 2000 aims to permanently remove a substantial amount from the previously planned annual operating cost structure of Telecom's core business so that after three years, previously planned annual operating costs should be substantially lower than they otherwise may have been," Deane said.
"The plan also aims to progressively remove $500 million from Telecom's previously planned capital expenditure programme between now and the end of the 1999/2000 financial year."
Deane said Telecom planned to handle calls faster by using sophisticated queue management systems and with better staff training.
"We also aim to reduce fault rates by more than 30 percent on average across all of New Zealand."
